title: Rollout incident follow-up: remediation playbook, evidence archive, and quick-safety controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: capture actionable follow-ups from the recent failed canary rollout, produce a compact remediation playbook for on-call, formalize a safety-check checklist for future rollouts, and create a searchable evidence archive for audits and learning.
comments: 2025-11-18 Maya Chen: Ticket created after the 2025-11-17 canary incident where model variant 'mosaic-v2-8q' regressed on hallucination rate and latency tail. Postmortem preliminary findings attached.

2025-11-20 Arjun Patel: Identified two immediate controls we can ship as hotfixes: (1) tighten canary traffic cap to 5% for first 12h, (2) add a realtime regression alert for hallucination score delta > 7% across golden prompt set. Filed PRs and monitoring changes below.

2025-11-24 Elena Ruiz (SRE): Ran chaos test against routing fallback; observed that auto-rollback margin did not trigger at 4.5% latency delta because metric window aggregated over 15m. Proposed change: add 3m short-window SLO for canary-phase only.
2025-11-28 Product review: PM sign-off on playbook structure; requested clearer owner handoff for post-rollback verification and customer comms template.

2025-12-02 Arjun Patel: Draft playbook uploaded to Confluence and PRs opened to implement short-window SLO and reduced initial canary weight. Requesting engineering review and approval before release.
2025-12-02 Maya Chen: Added requirement to archive request traces for first 1k canary requests to help root cause analysis for future incidents.
tasks: 1) Finalize remediation playbook with step-by-step rollback, verification, and customer-communication templates — owner: Arjun (due 2025-12-03)
2) Implement short-window (3m) SLO checks for canary phase and instrument as alert rule — owner: Elena (PR #4821)
3) Reduce initial canary weight to 5% and add staggered increases tied to alert-free windows — owner: Runtime Team (deploy runtime-1.20 canary config)
4) Add golden-prompt hallucination regression alert and dashboard panel; wire to page for P1 incidents — owner: Observability (due 2025-12-05)
5) Capture and persist first-1k canary request traces + anonymized payload archive for 30 days — owner: Privacy & Telemetry (compliance sign-off required)
6) Run tabletop drill with on-call + PM + SRE to validate playbook within cycle — owner: Maya (scheduled 2025-12-07)
7) Post-implementation review and close loop with affected customers using PM template — owner: Ariana (Customer Ops, due 2025-12-12)
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook contains clear step-by-step rollback + verification steps and is approved by on-call SRE and PM
Monitoring rules for short-window SLO and hallucination delta are deployed and firing in a test environment
Canary configuration updated to 5% initial weight and automated staged ramp implemented in runtime config
First-1k canary request traces are archived and accessible to incident investigators with audit logging
Tabletop drill completed and action items resolved or scheduled
resolution: In progress: short-window SLO and config change PRs open. Once monitoring PRs merge and tabletop drill succeeds we will move ticket to In Review then Done. Final postmortem evidence and learning log will be attached to the Confluence page for long-term retention.
